overview: Mexico is a large country in North America, between the United States and Central America. Its capital, Mexico City, is one of the biggest cities in the world. Mexico was home to great civilisations such as the Maya and the Aztecs, and it won independence from Spain in 1821. It has more Spanish speakers than any other country.

geography.text: Two mountain ranges, the Sierra Madre Occidental and the Sierra Madre Oriental, run down the country, with a high central plateau between them. A belt of volcanoes crosses central Mexico, including Pico de Orizaba, its highest peak. The north is mostly desert, the south has rainforests, and the flat limestone Yucatán Peninsula is dotted with natural sinkhole pools called cenotes.

history.text: Mexico was home to great civilisations, including the Olmecs, the Maya and the Aztecs, whose capital Tenochtitlan stood where Mexico City is now. Spain conquered the Aztecs in 1521. Mexico won independence in 1821, lost much of its northern territory to the United States in 1848, and went through a long revolution from 1910 to 1920.

events.title: Tenochtitlan founded
events.text: The Aztecs found their capital on an island in a lake.

events.title: War with the United States
events.text: Mexico loses about half its territory.

events.title: Mexican Revolution
events.text: A decade of revolution and civil war begins.

events.title: Olympics
events.text: Mexico City hosts the Summer Olympics.

government.text: Mexico is a federal presidential republic of 31 states and Mexico City. The President is elected for one six-year term and can never run again. In 2024 Claudia Sheinbaum became Mexico's first female President. Congress has a Chamber of Deputies and a Senate.

economy.text: Mexico has the second-largest economy in Latin America. It is a major manufacturer of cars, electronics and medical devices, most of which go to the United States, its biggest trading partner. Oil, silver, avocados, tomatoes and tourism are also important.

culture.text: Mexico has more native Spanish speakers than any other country. Its food, from tacos to mole, is listed by UNESCO. The Day of the Dead, when families honour relatives who have died with altars and marigolds, is world-famous. Painters Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera are Mexican.

items.title: Day of the Dead
items.text: Celebrated on 1 and 2 November, listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Chichén Itzá
items.text: A Maya city with a step pyramid built as a calendar.

items.title: Mariachi
items.text: Music played by bands in charro outfits, listed by UNESCO.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport. Mexico hosted the World Cup in 1970 and 1986 and co-hosted it in 2026, the first country to host three times. Lucha libre, masked professional wrestling, is hugely popular, and Mexico City hosted the 1968 Olympics.

items.text: The first country to host the men's World Cup three times.
Mexico City hosted the Summer Olympics.
